title: Inputs present and readable
attack: You are reporting numbers from files nobody can find.

title: Outcome distribution and the error brackets
attack: An R-squared of 0.67 on a variable with a narrow range is not an achievement.

title: Census of every multi-statistic field
attack: You found one striking pair and wrote a paper about it.

title: Learner and hyperparameter table
attack: You do not say what model this is or why it was chosen.

title: The two night-cooling constructions are not the same column
attack: Your two night-cooling variables are the same thing and you have counted it twice.

title: Frozen panels: what the model actually saw
attack: Nobody can reproduce this because nobody knows which columns survived your filters.

title: The formaldehyde pair before any model is fitted
attack: Everything you say about that pair is a property of your model, not of the air.

title: The located crossings, west and east
attack: Your thresholds are an average over two different climates and mean nothing in either.

title: Does the duration advantage follow atmospheric lifetime?
attack: You split twenty species at two days, which you chose, and got one-sided p = 0.006. Choose three days and tell me again.

title: Where the admission rules were placed
attack: Ninety-five per cent coverage and a cut at 0.98 are arbitrary and were chosen after you saw the result.

title: Five reference models
attack: You have not shown that any of this beats a regression.

title: Attribution surface for the threshold candidates
attack: You cannot locate a threshold without showing the curve.

title: Turning points, their intervals, and the gate swept
attack: Your stability gate is a rule you invented, placed where it gives the answer you wanted.

title: Whole-state holdout
attack: County-grouped folds still let the model learn the state it is predicting.

title: Residual spatial structure
attack: Your residuals are spatially autocorrelated, so your effective sample size is far smaller than three thousand counties.

title: Collinearity and interaction among the leading variables
attack: Eight of your fifteen leading variables have a variance inflation factor above ten.

title: Mutual information census: the same question with no model
attack: Your central finding is a TreeSHAP artefact.

title: Rank stability and the learning curve
attack: Your ranking is one draw. Resample and the top ten will be a different top ten.

title: Temporal validation: year holdout and forward chaining
attack: Every fold of yours contains the year it predicts. This is interpolation in time dressed as prediction.

title: Null calibration of the model's skill
attack: With 581 columns and repeated counties, 0.67 may be what your protocol returns on noise.

title: Does the crossing estimator find thresholds in noise?
attack: A smoothing spline will cross zero somewhere in anything. Your eleven thresholds are an artefact of the estimator.

title: Null for the census count
attack: Thirty-eight of forty-seven sounds impressive until you know what the null is.

title: The census under five attribution estimators
attack: Interventional TreeSHAP with a 500-row background is one choice among several and the result is a property of that choice.

title: Satellite only, environment only, everything admitted
attack: This is a socioeconomic model with satellite decoration, and you have not separated the two.

title: Leave-one-state-out jackknife of the census count
attack: Drop California and your 38 of 47 is 20 of 47.

title: Influence: drop the counties the model relies on most
attack: A hundred unusual counties are driving this.

title: Predictor perturbation and the located crossings
attack: These are reanalysis fields with their own error, and you report thresholds to three decimals.

title: What the admission gate is worth
attack: Your gate is a filter you tuned until the score looked right.

title: Formaldehyde pair: removal and inheritance
attack: Two columns correlated at 0.99 are one column. Drop either and nothing happens.

title: The band test
attack: If the pair is doing something a difference captures, say so and use the difference.

title: Every other pair above the correlation cut
attack: You have one anecdote and a mechanism invented to fit it.

title: Matched refit of the summary-statistic arms
attack: A ranking is not a prediction. Fit both and show me.

title: Drop one night-cooling construction and refit
attack: You kept both halves of a correlated pair. Show the cost of keeping only one.

title: Reproducibility by rerunning
attack: Gradient boosting is not deterministic and you have not shown this reproduces.

title: Multiplicity over the declared family
attack: You ran a great many tests and reported the ones that worked.
